newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Upward momentum intact on good bids.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Upward momentum intact on good bids.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market maintained their upward momentum on Thursday, well supported by aggressive demand from a local trading company, traders said.
The high sulphur fuel oil market rose by $1.00 per tonne after a firm purchase by a local trader shore up prices, they said.
A local trader bought from a Dutch trader a 20,000 tonne 180-centistoke cargo at $104 per tonne for loading April 15-19.
Traders said the local trader may be looking to buy more fuel oil cargo to satisfy potential demand in China.
The fuel oil swaps softened slightly but sentiment remained optimistic after the local trader emerged in the past few days with prompt physical demand.
The April swaps were at $102.00/$103.00, compared with Wednesday's $103.00/$104.00. May awaps slid to $100.00/$101.50 against $101.00/$102.00.
Most suppliers were unworried despite arbitrage cargoes arriving from the Mediterranean since the beginning of March.
"Since recent firm crude values have created a good environment, why not wait a little while for prices to rise further?" said another trader.
China is expected to import 400,000 tonnes of fuel oil in April compared to the estimated 600,000 tonnes in March.

Chinese traders said the cut in imports is primarily due to the gradual rise in spot prices in Singapore coupled with the increase in import tariffs to 6.0 percent from the previous 3.0 percent starting April 1.
But the reduced imports are not expected to dampen prices as supplies in Asia would be reduced during the same period, traders said.
Refinery turnarounds in China, Japan and South Korea would take away some lengths, they said.
However, some traders did not agree with the rally.
"It's all but a pricing games," said one.
"Prices may slumped once the game is over as it is artificially supported," another trader said.
In the LSWR market, demand from Japan remained slack and traders saw no signs of trading willingness to pick up. The Duri market remained competitive giving LSWR sellers a run for their money.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
